item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 20, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
At the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister of Singapore Gan Kim Yong, Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council Ding Xuexiang will visit Singapore from November 22 to 23, and co-chair with Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong the 22nd meeting of the China-Singapore Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation, the 27th meeting of the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park Joint Steering Council, the 18th meeting of the China-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City Joint Steering Council, and the 10th meeting of the China-Singapore (Chongqing) Demonstration Initiative on Strategic Connectivity Joint Steering Council. Xinhua News Agency: The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting was successfully held in Shenzhen. We notice that the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community put forward at the meeting has sparked heated discussion worldwide. Could you share more details on that? Guo Jiakun: On November 19, the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting was successfully held in Shenzhen. President Xi Jinping chaired the meeting and delivered important remarks, in which he elaborated on China’s proposals on building an Asia-Pacific community and announced China’s voluntary measures to support Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted the 2026 APEC Leaders’ Shenzhen Outlook—an ambitious, pragmatic and comprehensive document. This is the most important outcome of APEC “China Year,” and marks a new milestone in APEC cooperation. The Shenzhen Outlook focuses on four major areas “trade and economy, connectivity, innovation, and development,” and eight key aspects “Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, physical connectivity, institutional connectivity, people-to-people connectivity, digital economy, emerging technologies, capacity building, and sustainable growth,” setting up the pillars for building an Asia-Pacific community. The APEC members reaffirmed their commitment to APEC as the premier forum for regional economic cooperation, and to making continuous efforts to move toward the goal of building an Asia-Pacific community. They also extended their sincere appreciation to China, the host country, and the people and city of Shenzhen, Guangdong Province for their warm hospitality and thorough arrangements. China will work with Asia-Pacific partners to implement the common understandings reached at the meeting, work steadily toward the goal of Asia-Pacific community, strive for the wellbeing of the people in China and the Asia-Pacific, and make greater contributions to world peace and development. Asahi Shimbun: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said at a press conference in Shenzhen yesterday that the Japanese government’s position on the Taiwan question remains consistent with the 1972 Japan-China Joint Statement. She also indicated that there has been no change in the status of the four political documents between Japan and China, which serve as the foundational documents for bilateral relations. What is China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: Abiding by the four political documents between China and Japan is the political responsibility and legal obligation that Japan must fulfill. This should be not just reflected in remarks, but more importantly, implemented with concrete actions. For Japan, the pressing priority is to correct the erroneous words and moves on the Taiwan question immediately, adopt a correct attitude on historical issues, and form an objective and rational perception on China. JoongAng Ilbo: Yesterday the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia held a successful summit in Shenzhen. It’s reported that China said the three countries should maintain regular high-level exchanges. How would China respond if the U.S. were to host a second trilateral summit during the G20 Miami Summit next month? Guo Jiakun: The China-Russia-U.S. Summit was successfully held yesterday. China has released a readout, which you may refer to. AFP: The United Nations International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar is guilty of genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority. What is China’s comment on the ruling? Guo Jiakun: China has noted the judgment of the International Court of Justice. Given its complex historical, ethnic and religious dimensions, the Rakhine state issue needs to be resolved prudently through a holistic approach. The international community should make joint efforts to this end and avoid complicating the issue. China stands ready to continue supporting relevant parties in stepping up dialogue and consultation, and to play a constructive role in resolving the issue regarding the repatriation of the displaced people from Rakhine state. China believes international judicial institutions, as important instruments for upholding international fairness and justice, should exercise their powers with full prudence in accordance with law. China has concerns regarding such issues as ultra vires jurisdiction and overreach in interpretation, which are not conducive to the settlement of disputes. Global Times: The Chinese side just announced that Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang will visit Singapore and co-chair the mechanism meetings on bilateral cooperation. Could you share more information on this? Guo Jiakun: China and Singapore are friendly neighbors and important cooperation partners. Under the strategic guidance of the leaders of both sides, China-Singapore relations have maintained a sound momentum of growth, yielding fruitful outcomes in cooperation across various fields. President Xi Jinping just had an important meeting with Prime Minister Lawrence Wong this morning, charting the course for a new stage of development for bilateral ties. The mechanism meetings on bilateral cooperation are the apex platform coordinating collaboration between our two countries. China stands ready to work with Singapore to make good use of the meetings to deliver on our leaders’ strategic common understandings, formulate coordinated plans for cooperation in the next phase, unlock fresh impetus for the modernization drive in both countries, seek greater progress in our all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership, and contribute to development and prosperity in the region. AFP: This is a follow-up on the question about the International Court of Justice’s ruling on Myanmar. The Chinese ICJ jurist Xue Hanqin voted in Myanmar’s favor on all but one count. So my question is, was Ms. Xue acting on the instructions from the Chinese government? Guo Jiakun: The International Court of Justice is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations. Its judges serve in their individual capacity and perform their duties independently. Judge Xue Hanqin’s expression of her views is grounded in international law and the facts of the case, and informed by her expertise. This is consistent with the court’s established procedures and practices, and reflects the proper fulfillment of her responsibilities. Beijing Youth Daily: A total of ten foreign nationals received the Third Orchid Awards, according to selection results released by the Chinese side today. Would you like to comment on this? Guo Jiakun: We congratulate the laureates of the 2026 Orchid Awards. Hailing from all over the world, they share the same commitment to dispelling prejudice and nurturing understanding through cultural exchanges. Through decades of dedicated efforts, they have built bridges of friendship connecting the people of China and other countries. Established in 2022, the Orchid Awards have become an international cultural platform that delivers on the Global Civilization Initiative. China is ready to work with all parties to foster solidarity and enhance cooperation among different civilizations, cultures and peoples to seek common progress and build a community with a shared future for humanity. Asahi Shimbun: The China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace said that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. I have two questions. First, how would China define the “abuse” of jurisdiction? Second, what exactly do “other similar bodies” refer to? Guo Jiakun: On the International Criminal Court, China’s position is consistent, clear and above-board. China supports international judicial bodies in playing a constructive role for upholding international rule of law. That said, China stands that no international judicial body should violate the principle of state consent, abuse their jurisdiction, engage in politicization, or apply double standards.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 19, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Shenzhen TV: This morning, the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting was successfully held in Shenzhen. Could you share more details? Guo Jiakun: This morning, President Xi Jinping chaired the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting and delivered important remarks in Shenzhen. President Xi Jinping noted that the launch of APEC more than 30 years ago started a remarkable journey toward building an Asia-Pacific community. over three decades and more, the Asia-Pacific region has witnessed progress with each passing day, and created the Asia-Pacific miracle of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, we must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. President Xi Jinping stressed that China stands ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community: strengthen the pillar of economy and trade by aligning various regional economic and trade agreements and enhancing policy dialogue on the FTAAP; upgrade the pillar of connectivity by improving the infrastructure network, harmonizing policies and regulations, and facilitating travel for business, tourism and other purposes; foster the pillar of innovation by strengthening digital infrastructure development and encouraging the broad application of AI; enhance the pillar of development by promoting regional cooperation on energy and food security, achieving sustainable economic growth, supporting livelihood improvements, and investing in the people. President Xi announced new measures China would take to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, including providing financial support for APEC’s practical cooperation, establishing a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen, and setting up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy, and the development of SMEs. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC leaders’ declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. AFP: Some South Korean media outlets have reported today that there are no signs of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visiting China. Can the foreign ministry give us an indication of whether a meeting between Kim and U.S. President Donald Trump in China is being arranged? Guo Jiakun: I do not have information on that. Asahi Shimbun: Regarding the arrangements for the APEC events, the pared-down welcome accorded to the Japanese Prime Minister has been interpreted by some as a snub and drawn quite some attention. What’s China’s consideration behind such arrangements? Guo Jiakun: As the host, China makes appropriate protocol arrangements for all participants in accordance with international practice. AFP: Will the Chinese leader hold a meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi on the sidelines of the APEC summit? Guo Jiakun: Our position on China-Japan relations is clear.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 18, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
CCTV: The 2026 APEC CEO Summit is held in Shenzhen today, which is attended by many state leaders and people from the business communities. Can you share more details about this event? Guo Jiakun: This morning, President Xi Jinping attended the opening ceremony of the 2026 APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen and delivered a keynote speech, in which he made four propositions for jointly building an Asia-Pacific community and bringing prosperity for all in the region. First, upholding peace and stability. We should uphold the postwar international order and promote an equality-based and orderly multipolar world and economic globalization that is inclusive and brings benefit to all. We should resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, and overcome challenges through solidarity and cooperation. This is the way to cement the foundation for sustaining peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific. Second, building bridges of opening up and cooperation. We should firmly safeguard the WTO-centered, rules-based multilateral trading system, support free and open trade and investment, and keep global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded. We should work steadily toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific to pave the way for greater economic integration in the region. Third, boosting innovation to drive growth. We should forge science, technology and innovation partnerships, deepen cooperation in digital economy and AI, and promote green and low-carbon transition. By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific. Fourth, expanding our ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. We should remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy. At the same time, we should promote development that is balanced and delivers benefit to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness. We should follow a people-centered development philosophy, and ensure that development fruits are shared by all economies and all groups and communities. China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to help explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific. President Xi pointed out that China’s economy maintains a strong momentum of high-quality, innovation-driven growth, demonstrating great resilience and vitality. A blueprint for China’s development, the 15th Five-Year Plan also provides a list of opportunities for promoting economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. China will provide global business communities with a super-sized open market, a promising land for development, and an environment that enables mutually reinforcing cooperation. Asia-Pacific business communities are more than welcome to continue to get actively involved in China’s reform and opening up and modernization drive, and share in the opportunities created by Chinese modernization. AFP: Regarding tomorrow’s trilateral meeting between the three presidents of China, Russia and the U.S., will it cover Ukraine? Trump said before leaving for Asia that the leaders would talk about Ukraine. So would China shut down any discussion of Ukraine if it comes up? Guo Jiakun: The three heads of state will have an in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace. We will release information about the summit in a timely manner. Please check back for updates. The Hindu: I know you said previously that China hopes the meeting will focus on promoting strategic stability among the major powers. I was just wondering could you elaborate if are there any expectations of concrete outcomes that China hopes to see? Guo Jiakun: China has shared information on the China-Russia-U.S. Shenzhen Summit. The three heads of state will have an in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace. We will release information about the summit in a timely manner. Please check back for updates. AFP: The interim CEO of NVIDIA told shareholders yesterday that it was no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China, which means that the H200 chips that were previously allowed into China under a deal by Washington are no longer being sent over. Does China have a comment on this? Guo Jiakun: We have made clear more than once our principled position on U.S. chip exports to China.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 17, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Shenzhen TV: The APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting is set to be held in Shenzhen. Shenzhen has long been regarded as the window of China’s reform and opening up. Many western media coverage and vlogs on social media platforms portray Shenzhen as a “city of the future” and “an advanced city.” In recent days, robots, robotic dogs and AI agents on the streets of Shenzhen have drawn attention from guests at home and abroad. What is your comment on this? Guo Jiakun: We have noticed that many friends from the media are now using tech helpers such as AI smart glasses and smart studios in the APEC media center. As the third Chinese city hosting an APEC economic leaders’ meeting, Shenzhen has become a name card of China’s high-quality development and high-standard opening up, and witnessed the regional economic integration of the Asia Pacific. The 2026 APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting will soon kick off. China looks forward to working with all sides to further build consensus and deliver more practical outcomes, so as to inject strong impetus into the prosperity and growth of the Asia Pacific region and the world at large. Phoenix TV: On November 16, the U.S. Commerce Department released an interim final rule titled “Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors.” According to the rule, a license will be required to export advanced semiconductors to Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, or Brazil—countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion of chips to China. The aim is to prevent countries and companies subject to restrictions from gaining access to U.S. sensitive technologies. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: The move is yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry. Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains. China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate rights and interests. Yonhap News Agency: On November 16 local time, U.S. President Donald Trump said that he might meet with President of the State Affairs of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) Kim Jong Un in China, but that it was still unclear whether President Kim would come or not, adding that it was up to China. What’s China’s comment on President Trump’s remarks? Is there any possibility that the DPRK and the United States will hold talks? (Similar Question from Reuters) Guo Jiakun: We do not have information on that. EFE: The visa-free policy for countries including Spain, France and Germany expires at the end of this year. Will China extend it, and when can we expect an announcement? Guo Jiakun: China attaches high importance to facilitating people-to-people exchange with other countries and is assessing relevant policies. AFP: The U.S. government is investigating Singapore-based firm MegaSpeed for whether it helped shift NVIDIA’s most powerful technology to Chinese firms in violation of U.S. export restrictions. Does China have a comment on the investigation and is China aware of any firms within China that had obtained this technology from MegaSpeed? Guo Jiakun: I just answered a question relating to this subject. I need to stress that China’s position on U.S. chip exports to China is consistent.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on November 16, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
CCTV: To follow up on the announcement of the China-Russia-U.S. Shenzhen Summit, could you share with us the detailed arrangement and China’s expectation? Mao Ning: This will be the first ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. heads of state. The three presidents will have an in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and enabling strategic stability in major-country relations. The summit is of groundbreaking significance. China, Russia, and the U.S. are founding members of the United Nations and permanent members of the Security Council. In history, the three countries fought side by side to win the World Anti-Fascist War. Under the current circumstances, the three countries shoulder important responsibilities to work together in addressing global challenges and promoting world peace and stability. It is in the interest of the three countries to strengthen communication, manage differences and maintain stable relations. This is also the expectation of the international community and is conducive to global stability and dialogue and cooperation. CGTN: Recently, Chinese special envoys and special representative visited countries in the Middle East, the Gulf region, the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa. Could you share more details? Mao Ning: Recently, Special Envoy of the Chinese Government on the Middle East Issue Zhai Jun, Special Representative of the Chinese Government on African Affairs Liu Xianfa, and Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa Affairs of the Foreign Ministry Hu Changchun visited a total of seven countries in the Middle East, the Gulf region and the Horn of Africa. It is a major diplomatic effort taken by China, under the guidance of the initiatives and propositions on promoting peace and stability in the Middle East and the four principles on the constructive participation of relevant parties in the resolution of African hotspot issues put forward by President Xi Jinping, to ease tensions in the region, and bring an end to hostilities. During the visits, the special envoys and special representative have met with relevant countries’ leaders, foreign ministers and other officials in charge of foreign affairs and national security. They engaged in friendly exchanges on deepening bilateral relations, had comprehensive and in-depth exchanges of views on promoting deescalation of regional hotspot and sensitive issues, and reached a number of common understandings regarding strengthening solidarity and collaboration, safeguarding peace, and promoting development. As a permanent member of the UN Security Council and a major responsible country, China is committed to supporting, promoting, and safeguarding world peace and development. On addressing challenges to peace and security and the hotspot issues in the Middle East and Africa, China always stands shoulder to shoulder with Middle Eastern and African people, stands for peace and cooperation, and stands on the right side of history. China will work with regional countries and the international community to implement the Global Security Initiative, follow the new vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, and continue playing a constructive role in achieving enduring peace and security, development and prosperity in the Middle East and Africa. NHK: Regarding the China-Russia-U.S. Summit, the U.S. side indicated that topics such as nuclear arms control and the situation in Iran will be discussed. Could you specify which issues China plans to raise during the meeting? Furthermore, could you provide more details on any bilateral meetings that China may have scheduled with countries such as Russia and Japan? Mao Ning: The three heads of state will have an in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace. We will release information about the summit in a timely manner. Please check back for updates. Regarding the bilateral meetings on the sidelines of APEC, I have no information to share at the moment. Beijing Daily: The international community is paying close attention to the evolving situation in the Middle East and the Gulf region and attaching high importance to China’s role there. Could you share more information on the trip to regional countries by the Special Envoy of the Chinese Government on the Middle East Issue? Mao Ning: Special Envoy Zhai Jun visited Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia, where he had in-depth exchanges with relevant parties over the situation in Iran and Yemen. He elaborated on China’s positions and propositions and worked actively to promote peace and facilitate talks, contributing to efforts towards bringing about a deescalation in the Gulf region and a political settlement of the Yemen issue. Relevant parties spoke highly of President Xi Jinping’s initiatives and propositions on promoting peace and stability in the Middle East, and commended China’s constructive role in promoting peace and security in the region. The most pressing task at hand, they believe, is to rebuild trust as soon as possible, bring the temperature down, and prevent a resumption of fighting. They look to the international community to pool greater synergy and help deescalate the situation. China will continue to be guided by President Xi Jinping’s initiatives and propositions and facilitate a dynamism where parties stay committed to dialogue and consultation, work to bridge differences, accommodate each other’s concerns and build consensus on peace. We will support regional countries in jointly creating a new regional architecture for common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, and join international efforts to bring about the early restoration of peace and tranquility in the region. Beijing Daily: Did Special Envoy Zhai Jun have contact with the Houthis during his visit? Mao Ning: While visiting regional countries, Special Envoy Zhai Jun had communication with various parties of the Yemen issue on the situation in the country. China supports the political settlement of the Yemen issue, calls for upholding the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of Yemen, and hopes to see security and stability restored in the country at an early date. China will continue playing a constructive role to this end. China News Service: From November 9 to 11, the Institute of Japanese Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Exhibition Hall of Evidences of Crime Committed by Unit 731 of the Imperial Japanese Army co-hosted the Symposium on the Atrocities of the Imperial Japanese Army’s Bacteriological and Chemical Warfare in Harbin. Do you have any comment? Mao Ning: During World War II, the Imperial Japanese Army conducted bacteriological and chemical warfare, which inflicted untold suffering on the Chinese people and constitutes heinous crimes against humanity. To this day, Japan’s abandoned chemical weapons (ACWs) in China continue to pose a serious threat to the health and safety of the Chinese people and the environment in affected regions. Japan committed innumerable and undeniable crimes during its militarist aggression. We urge Japan to deeply reflect on its war crimes, fully and faithfully fulfill its responsibility and obligations under the Chemical Weapons Convention and the MOU between the two countries’ governments, including thoroughly removing the hazardous ACWs as soon as possible, so that the Chinese people no longer have to live on soil tainted by ACWs, and earn the trust of its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions. Bloomberg: The U.S. signed an agreement with nine other parties on AI-related supply chain. Do you think this agreement will have any impact on the upcoming meeting between Chinese and U.S. presidents? Will China bring up this agreement in the meeting? Mao Ning: China believes that artificial intelligence is a shared asset of humanity, and that there should be no drawing lines along ideological differences or forming exclusive groupings. All parties should work together for the development and governance of AI, so that it can better serve the common welfare of humanity. As for the meeting between the two presidents, the two sides are in communication.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on November 13, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Xinhua News Agency: To follow up on China’s announcement about President Xi Jinping’s attendance at the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting and related events, could you share more details and China’s expectation of the meeting? Mao Ning: After 12 years, China is once again hosting APEC. We have had a fruitful APEC “China Year” so far. Together with other member economies of APEC, by focusing on the theme of “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together” and the three priority areas of “Openness, Innovation, and Cooperation,” China has successfully held over 300 meetings and events, including the APEC senior officials’ meetings, 10 ministerial meetings on women, trade, tourism, forestry, food security, SMEs, energy, human resources, transportation and finance, and high-level events of the Digital Weeks. More than 10,000 representatives have participated in the events and reached a number of common understandings on cooperation, laying a solid foundation for the upcoming APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen. Next week, the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting will kick off in Shenzhen. We look forward to building further consensus and agreeing on the APEC Shenzhen Leaders’ Declaration among all member economies as well as more practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, AI and so on to inject strong impetus into the prosperity and growth of the Asia Pacific and the world. Bloomberg: CNN has reported that the U.S. intelligence community is still working to understand the relationship between a Chinese business woman who had an affair with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and the Chinese government, with multiple sources telling CNN that the intelligence collected on her does not prove that she was acting as a spy for Beijing, and the characterization of Alice Huang as the Chinese spy is over-torqued. We’re wondering if the foreign ministry has a comment. Mao Ning: We have made our position clear regarding the so-called “Chinese spy” allegation. The Paper: As the curtain fell on the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai, we have seen new records in terms of the number of exhibitors, exhibition floor space and the value of intended deals. Over a hundred enterprises and institutions have signed up for the next edition. The expo has been described as an “importathon.” What is your comment on this? Mao Ning: As the world’s second-largest consumer and import market, China has held the CIIE for nine consecutive years. Our doors are wide open to the world for sharing development opportunities. At this year’s expo, businesses from all over the world once again cast a yes vote on and showed their confidence and desire to further cultivate the Chinese market. The appeal of the Chinese market comes from its enormous size and potential as well as China’s institutional strengths. Policy predictability, an increasingly business-friendly environment and a more robust legal framework provide the strongest reassurance. China will work to ensure the continued success of the CIIE, stand for openness and win-win cooperation, and through China’s sustained high-quality development, provide more certainty for global development. PTI: You already outlined the importance of the forthcoming APEC summit. I just would like you to highlight what will be the most important expectation in terms of global importance that China expects out of this summit. Mao Ning: The theme for the APEC “China Year” is “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together.” We look forward to working with all parties to adopt the Shenzhen Declaration at next week’s APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting, and achieve practical outcomes in areas that are vital for both regional and global economic growth, such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, and artificial intelligence. AFP: Two questions. Firstly, on APEC again, just since it’s only a few days away, now I wondered if you had any update on the potential trilateral meeting between the presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia. And then a second question, on the report yesterday in the Guardian that said that China has ruled out hosting the COP33 climate summit in 2028. I wonder if you could tell if that’s correct. And if so, why does China not want to host COP33? Mao Ning: On your first question, China is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state. If there is further information, we will release it in a timely way. On your second question, we have no information at the moment. The Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change is an important platform for global climate governance. China is committed to advancing global green and low-carbon transition and international cooperation on climate response. Bloomberg: Bloomberg has reported that banned NVIDIA chips ended up at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, who is reportedly in Beijing. What is the foreign ministry’s comment? And the second question is that U.S. lawmakers and the Commerce Department are moving quickly to advance new chip bills and block Chinese firms from remotely accessing American computing power overseas. Does Beijing view these potential restrictions as a violation of the U.S.-China trade truce ahead of next week’s APEC summit, and how would China respond? Mao Ning: On your first question, I am not familiar with the situation. On your second question, China opposes abuse of export control measures, which disrupt the stability of global industrial and supply chains and serve no one’s interests. China and the U.S. need to work together to deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents and uphold the momentum of steady development of China-U.S. economic and trade ties. Bloomberg: What action is China prepared to take in response to Thailand’s concerns that mining operations involving Chinese companies in Myanmar may be contributing to arsenic contamination in the rivers flowing into Thailand, including whether Beijing will investigate the companies involved? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with the specifics. The Chinese government has all along asked Chinese companies to fulfil their corporate responsibility and protect the environment. We stand ready to enhance cooperation with Thailand and other Mekong countries on the protection of water resources and ecological environment.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on November 12, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
As agreed between China and the ROK, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the ROK Cho Hyun will visit China from November 13 to 14. China News Service: Today marks the 78th anniversary of the verdict of the International Military Tribunal for the Far East (also known as the Tokyo Trials). Do you have any comment? Mao Ning: Seventy-eight years ago today, after two and a half years of trial proceedings, with abundant solid evidence and rigorous legal basis, the Tokyo Trials found Japanese militarists guilty of waging the war of aggression and severely violating the international law, and brought 25 Class-A war criminals to justice, bringing to light their crimes and condemning them to perpetual infamy. The Tokyo Trials are an integral part of the postwar international order. Recognizing and accepting the judgement of the Tokyo Trials is the prerequisite for Japan’s postwar return to the international community. However, to people’s indignation, for many years, Japanese right-wing forces still turn a blind eye to the historic verdict of the Tokyo Trials, try every possible means to deny and even glorify the crimes committed during the war of aggression, and promote a distorted view of history. It is alarming that, in recent years, the Japanese government, who is reluctant to make a clean break with militarism, has been boosting military expenditure, developing offensive capabilities, promoting the revision of the three security documents, attempting to ditch the three non-nuclear principles, and quickening the pace of rearming itself. Those moves severely challenge the fundamental legal principles laid down by the Trials, and threaten the peace and stability in the region. History shall not be forgotten. Justice shall not be challenged. The international community should work together to reject the retrogressive moves to reverse the historic verdict and revive militarism. China will work with all peace-loving countries and people to firmly uphold historical truth, safeguard postwar international order, and defend international fairness and justice. BBC: Is China concerned that the NVIDIA spy scandal will affect U.S.-China relations ahead of the likely summit between the two presidents next week? How would China react if it resulted in the U.S. further restricting technology exports to China? Mao Ning: On the so-called “Chinese spy,” we have made our position clear. China’s sci-tech progress relies on independent innovation and open cooperation. The U.S. should stop fabricating the “Chinese spy” narratives as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions. China and the U.S. maintain close communication on heads-of-state interactions. We are ready to work the U.S. side to deliver on the important common understandings reached between the two presidents and jointly build a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity. Reuters: Are you able to provide any updates on a potential meeting between the presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia at next week’s APEC summit? Mao Ning: China is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state. If there is further information, we will release it in a timely way. CNR: Belgium and Chile announced on November 6 that they have decided to join their candidatures for hosting the seat of the Secretariat of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement). This joint candidature provides for the Secretariat being based in the city of Valparaíso, Chile, the Clearing-House Mechanism will be installed in and operating from Brussels, and Brussels will host the meetings of the subsidiary bodies. Does China have any comment on this? Mao Ning: Earlier this year, China nominated Xiamen to bid for the seat of the Secretariat of the BBNJ Agreement. The candidature has quickly received the support of the majority of the Parties to the Agreement. On November 6, without prior consultation with the Parties to the Agreement, Belgium and Chile announced the decision to join their candidatures for the seat of the Secretariat. This joint candidature provides for the Secretariat being based in the city of Valparaíso, Chile, the Clearing-House Mechanism (CHM) will be installed in and operating from Brussels, and Brussels will host the meetings of the subsidiary bodies. By seeking an unauthorized backroom deal on issues that should be determined by the Conference of the Parties (COP), the joint candidature is problematic in at least six aspects. First, it contravenes the stipulations of the BBNJ Agreement. According to the Agreement, the seat of the Secretariat, the specific modalities for the operation of the CHM, including its installation, as well as where the subsidiary bodies hold their meetings shall all be determined by COP, and the CHM shall be managed by the Secretariat. Belgium and Chile traded under the table what should be collectively determined by all Parties to the Agreement. This is a violation of the stipulations of the Agreement and an act of disrespect to the authority of COP. Second, it contravenes procedural justice. The choice of the Secretariat seat and the development of the CHM are two items of different nature scheduled to be collectively determined by COP through separate decisions. The Belgium-Chile proposal bundles the two together in an attempt to force it as a package upon other Parties. This is against applicable procedural rules and a hijack of the Parties’ will. Third, it contravenes established international practice. The management of the CHM is a key mandate of the Secretariat. In the practice established by other international treaties like the Convention on Biological Diversity, the secretariats and CHMs are located in the same place. The Belgium-Chile proposal, which locates the Secretariat and the CHM separately across the ocean, will without a doubt raise the operation cost, lower management efficiency, and increase the financial burden on the Parties to the Agreement. Fourth, it contravenes equitable geographical distribution. The vast majority of major global institutions are based in Europe, with none located in Asia. Developing countries have been calling on global institutions to redress this long-existing injustice and bring about greater fairness and equity. Brussels is already home to the headquarters of NATO and the EU. If this non-coastal city were to host the CHM of an ocean-related treaty as well, it would further widen the digital divide to the detriment of the shared interests of the Global South. Fifth, it contravenes fair competition. The BBNJ Secretariat is tasked with contributing to global ocean governance. The selection of its seat should be a fair and friendly process in keeping with the rules. The Belgium-Chile proposal, however, politicizes the bidding process and attempts to divide Parties into camps. It not only undermines the principle of fair, friendly and healthy competition, but also negates the essence of multilateralism. Sixth, it contravenes the original commitment. Chile first made the bid citing its significance for the Global South. Yet according to the new proposal, Chile will no longer assume the substantive functions of the Secretariat. Belgium, for its part, only seeks to host the CHM and thereby has in effect relinquished its bid for the Secretariat seat. I wish to stress that the adoption and entry into force of the BBNJ Agreement is a victory of multilateralism. Its implementation likewise needs to serve and advance the common well-being of all humanity. We call on the international community to find a home for the Secretariat best positioned for its efficient operation and the effective implementation of the Agreement. China firmly supports multilateralism and the cause of the UN, and is committed to promoting and improving global ocean governance. As one of the first signatories and Parties to the Agreement and the largest assessed-contributor to its budget, China has the will, capability and confidence to provide strong support and backing for the operation of the Secretariat. China is fully ready. We look forward to working with all Parties to the Agreement to keep selection of the Secretariat seat proceeding in the right direction, and uphold the overall and fundamental interests of the international community, especially those of developing countries. Reuters: China’s increasingly assertive actions in the waters east of Taiwan threaten regional stability and freedom of navigation, G7 foreign ministers said in a joint declaration published yesterday following a meeting in Paris. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on this statement? Mao Ning: We have taken note of this joint declaration. China’s position on Taiwan and other issues is consistent, clear, justified and above-board. The statement you mentioned disregards facts, grossly interferes in China’s internal affairs and maliciously smears China, while turning a blind eye to China’s contribution to world peace, stability and development. There is no truth in the assertions, which serves as further proof that the G7 is an ideological group with entrenched Cold War mentality and stuck in the rut of bloc politics. In no way can such a grouping represent the international community. The G7 should focus on its own business, step up to its responsibilities, and play a positive role in tackling the pressing challenges of our times and enhancing international solidarity. AFP: Could you tell us if in the talks yesterday, Wang Yi and Marco Rubio discussed nuclear arms control, and the prospect of including it in the agenda of the potential trilateral meeting between China, Russia and the U.S. next week? Mao Ning: On yesterday’s phone call between Foreign Minister Wang Yi and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, China has released a readout. I have no more information to add. Yonhap News Agency: To follow up on the upcoming visit of Minister of Foreign Affairs of the ROK, could you please share more information about what will be discussed? Mao Ning: China and the ROK are each other’s important neighbors and cooperation partners. Late last year and early this year, President Xi Jinping and President Lee Jae Myung visited each other’s countries successfully, ushering China-ROK relations into a new stage of improvement and growth. China attaches great importance to Minister Cho Hyun’s visit, and stands ready to work with the ROK side to deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents, have in-depth exchanges of views on our bilateral relationship and issues of mutual interest, and promote the sustained, steady and sound development of the China-ROK strategic cooperative partnership. AFP: Procurement notices from the Northwestern Polytechnical University in Xi’an show that the university bought several NVIDIA H200 chips, despite them being restricted on the U.S. export controls. I wonder if you could tell us any more about that and what the chips might have been bought for? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with the specifics you mentioned. China’s position on U.S. chips export to China is consistent. China firmly opposes the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security and formulating various types of discriminatory lists to go after Chinese institutions. Bloomberg: Sources say MegaSpeed International founder Alice Huang is currently living in Beijing. We are wondering if the foreign ministry could confirm this and comment? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with that.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on the 7.6 Magnitude Earthquake in Panama
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Q: It’s reported that a 7.6 magnitude earthquake struck Panama on October 10, followed by over 100 aftershocks. What is China’s comment? A: China expresses sympathies to the Panamanian government and people in the affected region. As of now, there is no report of casualties involving Chinese nationals in the earthquake. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Chinese Embassy in Panama will continue to closely monitor the situation and promptly provide necessary assistance to Chinese nationals in need. We remind Chinese nationals in Panama to take precautions against secondary hazards caused by the earthquake.
